source.version: Journal abstract only (Europe PMC PMID 41436597; Crossref metadata: Nature Human Behaviour 10(3):531-540, published online 2025-12-23). Journal full text not obtained: the Nature article page returned a client challenge. Separately read all 27 pages of the older PsyArXiv draft in memory: xeh64_v1, dat_main_241124.pdf, file version 2, modified 2024-12-04 according to OSF file metadata; https://osf.io/download/9utcm/. The PDF is titled 'A large-scale evaluation of the collaborative potential of human and machine creativity' (p. 1) and has materially different prompting results (pp. 10-11). The studies and findings below remain based on the journal abstract; the older draft is not substituted for the journal version.
source.title_on_document: A large-scale comparison of divergent creativity in humans and large language models

paper_design_summary: The journal abstract compares human and LLM output on an established creativity task that it does not name, reporting 9,198 humans and 215,542 LLM observations for the research as a whole. It also describes model-only manipulations using genius personas, demographic roles, and strategic prompt engineering, without allocating LLM observations across outcomes or prompting conditions. No person is described as receiving AI help.

studies.label: Humans versus LLMs on an established creativity task

participants.who: Humans (N = 9,198) compared with LLM output; 215,542 is the journal abstract-level LLM observation count for the research as a whole, with no allocation to outcomes or prompting conditions. The abstract does not describe the human sample, name the LLMs, or state the country.
participants.quote: Here we compare the ability of humans (N = 9,198) and large language models (LLMs, N = 215,542 observations) to generate novel ideas in an established creativity task.

eligibility.reason: The journal abstract compares separately generated human and LLM output and describes model-only prompting, with no random assignment of people to AI assistance (Europe PMC PMID 41436597, abstract sentences 2 and 6). Its human sample meets the people-count threshold (N = 9,198, sentence 2), and creativity is evaluated on generated ideas (sentences 2 and 4-6). The paper therefore remains ai_vs_human context evidence, not core; the prompting study is model-only. The journal full text remains unavailable. The older PsyArXiv draft was reviewed separately and describes the same broad comparative and model-only designs (pp. 4-11, Results; pp. 14-15, Methods), but does not establish the journal version's detailed methods or outcome counts.

one_line_finding: The journal abstract reports slightly higher average creativity and greater variability and upper-tail creativity among humans than LLMs (9,198 humans and 215,542 LLM observations across the research, with outcome-specific LLM counts unstated); persona prompts raised LLM creativity up to a threshold, while strategic prompt engineering yielded mixed to negative results (Europe PMC PMID 41436597, abstract sentences 2 and 4-6; no numerical effect sizes provided).
notes: Journal results are abstract-only. The journal abstract does not name the creativity task, scoring method, LLMs, or human sample, so measure remains not_stated (outside the form's listed values) rather than inferred. The separately read older PsyArXiv draft names the Divergent Association Task and describes automated scoring (pp. 3 and 14-15), but these details have not been verified in the journal full text. Its prompting findings differ materially: perspective-taking prompts improved DAT scores and creative-genius prompts reduced them (p. 10, Studies 3A and 3B), whereas the journal abstract reports mixed-to-negative strategic prompting and persona/role gains up to a threshold (sentence 6). Do not combine these versions. All 27 pages of the older PDF were read in memory; there is no local markdown or PDF for this record. That draft references supplementary Tables S5-S8 (p. 5) and Note 1 in SI (p. 10); the supplementary information is not included in the PDF and was not obtained. The source.supplement fields remain unconfirmed for the journal version.
